interest: 1930s Canadian spy scare over Japanese in British Columbia.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.20242) documents intelligence reports, diplomatic despatches, cross-reference sheets, and press clippings compiled by United States consular and diplomatic missions in Canada between 1932 and 1937 concerning alleged Japanese military activities, espionage, surveillance, and propaganda. The file traces early consular monitoring of competing Chinese and Japanese propaganda campaigns in Victoria, British Columbia, in 1932; detailed investigations in 1936 into two Japanese aviation representatives suspected of conducting covert military surveillance and technical photography at airfields in Edmonton and Winnipeg; and the intense public controversy that erupted in late 1937 following sensational allegations by Canadian wartime padre Archdeacon F. G. Scott that disguised Japanese naval officers and converted 'mystery ships' were operating along the British Columbia coastline. Through diplomatic assessments, Canadian press coverage, official statements from Canadian Defence Minister Ian Mackenzie and Vancouver civic authorities, and formal rebuttals by the Japanese Legation, the file illuminates the growing security anxieties, commercial frictions, and defense planning along the Pacific rim of North America prior to the Second World War.

subfiles.about: Report on concurrent Japanese and Chinese press propaganda in Victoria, British Columbia, and local public attitudes toward Japanese aggression in the Orient.
subfiles.summary: Bucklin reports Japanese and Chinese propaganda side by side in the Victoria Daily Colonist, the Japanese seen as unfriendly to the U.S.
subfiles.title: Despatch from George A. Bucklin on Japanese and Chinese Propaganda in Victoria, B.C.

subfiles.about: Report on suspected intelligence gathering by visiting Japanese aviation officials at the Edmonton airport and South Cooking Lake seaplane base.
subfiles.summary: Medalie reports that Japanese visitors K. Owago and H. Saito took over 200 photos of Edmonton's airport, suggesting military aims.
subfiles.title: Despatch from D. P. Medalie on Japanese Aviation Officials at Edmonton Airport

subfiles.about: Report that the two Japanese aviation officials previously investigated in Edmonton also conducted an examination of the airport in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
subfiles.summary: Kemp reports that the same Japanese visitors inspected Winnipeg airport on April 24, 1936.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 76 from Edwin C. Kemp on Japanese Aviation Officials at Winnipeg Airport

subfiles.about: Comprehensive diplomatic report detailing the public controversy and political fallout surrounding Archdeacon Scott's allegations of Japanese espionage in British Columbia.
subfiles.summary: American Minister Norman Armour reports on the nationwide sensation caused by Archdeacon F. G. Scott's claims that disguised Japanese naval officers and mystery ships were operating in British Columbia. Armour summarizes public rebuttals, including an open letter from Japanese Naval Attaché Commander K. Takeuchi denouncing the claims as malicious fabrications and guarded statements by Defence Minister Ian Mackenzie regarding Canadian intelligence vigilance. The report also highlights dismissive reactions from Vancouver Mayor George C. Miller and Police Chief W. W. Foster, alongside an Ottawa Journal editorial arguing that Canada possessed no military secrets worth the cost of foreign espionage.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1744 from Norman Armour on British Columbia Japanese Spy Scare

subfiles.about: Press clipping reporting Archdeacon F. G. Scott's interview alleging disguised Japanese naval officers and mystery ships on the British Columbia coast.
subfiles.summary: Winnipeg Tribune report of Archdeacon F. G. Scott's claim that disguised Japanese naval officers lived in B.C. fishing villages.
subfiles.title: Clipping from the Winnipeg Tribune: 'Padre Asserts Jap Officers in Disguise in B.C.'

subfiles.about: Published open letter by the Japanese Naval Attaché refuting Archdeacon Scott's claims of disguised naval officers and mystery ships in British Columbia.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Naval Attaché Takeuchi calls Archdeacon Scott's spy charges groundless and malicious.
subfiles.title: Clipping from the Ottawa Citizen: 'Japanese Answer to Archdeacon' by Commander K. Takeuchi

subfiles.about: Press report on Defence Minister Ian Mackenzie's statements regarding Pacific coastal surveillance and Canadian rearmament projects.
subfiles.summary: Defence Minister Ian Mackenzie says his department is well informed on the coast, and announces RCAF aircraft orders.
subfiles.title: Clipping from the Daily Colonist: 'Says Department Is Kept Well Informed On Coastal Matters'

subfiles.about: Press article examining coastal espionage fears, potential Canadian-American intelligence exchanges, and reactions from Vancouver municipal authorities.
subfiles.summary: Toronto Star reports possible Canada-U.S. intelligence exchange on Japanese fishing boats; Vancouver officials blamed the spy scare on economic resentment.
subfiles.title: Clipping from the Toronto Daily Star: 'May Exchange Data on 'Spying' With U.S. Is Belief at Capital'

subfiles.about: Editorial ridiculing the Japanese spy scare and asserting that Canada possesses no military secrets that would justify foreign espionage.
subfiles.summary: Ottawa Journal editorial mocks the spy scare, saying Canada has no secrets worth stealing.
subfiles.title: Clipping from the Ottawa Journal: 'Why Spy on Canada?'

subfiles.summary: File note and extract on Japanese timber fronts in British Columbia, Mackenzie's statements and Japanese denials of espionage.
subfiles.title: Document File Note and Extract from Despatch No. 1760 on Japanese Activities in British Columbia
